cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-drawn batik kemben (breast-cloth) with soga and indigo dyeing, tritik and lidah api motifs — a textile form and technique characteristic of Javanese dress.

physical.title: breast-cloth
physical.summary: A woman's cotton (tabby) batik breast-cloth, a 'kemben'; hand-drawn on both sides.  Dyed in soga (brown) and indigo.  Rectangular blue panel in centre echoed in ever-widening bands.  The central panel is edged with 'tritik' (sewn tie-dye) pattern.  Surrounding this panel is a row of inward-pointing flame ('lidah api') motifs.  Those on the long sides sloping towards the middle of the cloth, in black and soga against a cream ground, within a rectangular border of spade shapes, alternately pointing up or down.  Outside this is a narrow border of wavy lines in white dots against a blue ground.  Narrow 'sisir' strips along long sides and short ends, outside an inner border of more complex narrower sisir stripes.  Star design at each corner.  Veining produced by 'remukkan process', in which the wax has been deliberately cracked to allow the dye to seep through, in the 'lidah api' and spade pattern sections. Hemmed on one long side and both short ends. Small area of damage at one corner.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
